messages:
maria-cs: Quick heads-up — Helio asked to cap monthly usage at 250k tokens and shorten renewal to 9 months. They proposed -10% off list if we accept. Procurement says they will pay via PO but need vendor code + updated SOW showing prorate. Legal/Finance guidance please? Also procurement claims EU entity requires wet signature not DocuSign.
josh-sales: looping in @sarah-legal and @oliver-finance. From a sales/ARR view we prefer 12mo, but can consider 9mo with stricter payment terms. Can we do prorated pricing + smaller discount (e.g., -5%) and protect ARR? :thinking_face:
tina-csm: context: they are still in onboarding and haven’t hit steady-state usage. They want the cap to avoid surprise bills. If we accept a cap we need clear overage rules and reporting cadence. I can show usage profile so they see expected cost.
sarah-legal: I can draft an amendment. Quick Q: is the EU wet-signature requirement absolute or negotiable (can they sign via their US parent)? We prefer DocuSign — faster and auditable. If wet is required we need to check local acceptance and add a clause.
oliver-finance: vendor code / invoicing checklist: we need billing entity, VAT, PO number to match invoice. If they want net60 we should ask for partial upfront on a shortened term. Also we won't issue a vendor code until legal signals contract is final.
maria-cs: Billing entity per client: "Helio EU Ltd" (VAT FR123456). Procurement said this will come with a PO by Friday and they asked for net60. They want the -10% discount tied to the 9mo ask. Can we push net30?
josh-sales: +1 to pushing net30. Proposal: offer -5% + a month-1 usage credit instead of -10. That keeps revenue higher and is an easier sell. If they insist on net60, require 50% upfront on 9mo. :thumbsup:
sarah-legal: ok I can add amendment language: discount contingent on signed amendment + PO, cap set to 250k tokens, overages billed at $0.0004/token (example). I'll draft and aim for EOD.
tina-csm: I'll assemble two example invoices showing cost under cap and under expected overage so they can see the delta. That should reassure procurement.
oliver-finance: if they insist on net60, finance wants 50% upfront for 9 months; otherwise standard net30. We'll also need the PO to reference invoice matching rules. Sample PO field they might use: `PO: 2026-HE-0098`.
maria-cs: About DocuSign vs wet: client says local EU team insists on wet for entity signing. @sarah-legal — can we accept wet if US parent signs as guarantor?
sarah-legal: wet is possible but needs a guarantor clause from US parent and adds cycle time. Recommend asking client to sign via DocuSign first; include a wet-sign exception if legal insists. I'll draft both options in the amendment.
deploy-bot: Reminder: renewal flag set in CRM for Helio; playbook step: CSM attach amendment doc to opportunity and set follow-up for PO.
josh-sales: I'll negotiate for -5% + month1 credit and request they route the PO to US parent. If routing fails, we'll accept net60 only with the 50% upfront. Recommend DocuSign to speed this.
maria-cs: Action items: @sarah-legal draft amendment (EOD), @oliver-finance confirm vendor code & invoicing process once legal signs, @tina-csm prepare usage examples, @josh-sales hold the discount negotiation. I'll follow up with client about PO routing. Thanks all.
maria-cs: Update (next day): client agreed to DocuSign for initial signature; procurement will send PO by Friday. @sarah-legal can you prioritize the amendment?
sarah-legal: On it — I'll post first draft in ~3 hours and include docsign + wet exception language.
